description: Canonical seed knowledge base for the AI Software Development Factory.

patterns.name: ReAct
patterns.description: An agent alternates between reasoning about the current problem and taking actions through tools, then uses the observations to decide the next step.
patterns.intent: Enable an agent to iteratively reason, act, observe results, and continue until it has enough evidence or reaches a useful outcome.
when_to_use: The task requires iterative investigation.
The agent needs external tools or APIs to gather information.
The next action depends on the result of a previous action.
when_not_to_use: The task is a simple deterministic transformation.
No tools or iterative reasoning are required.
A fixed sequence of steps is sufficient.
prerequisites: An LLM capable of tool/function calling
strengths: Can adapt actions based on observations
weaknesses: Requires strong stopping and error handling
references: Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

patterns.name: Reflection
patterns.description: An agent generates an output and then evaluates its own work to identify weaknesses and improve the result.
patterns.intent: Improve output quality by explicitly evaluating and revising an initial result.
when_to_use: Quality can be improved through self-critique.
The output has measurable or inspectable weaknesses.
A second pass is cheaper than recovering from a poor final result.
when_not_to_use: The task is trivial.
There is no useful signal for evaluating the output.
Latency or token cost is extremely constrained.
weaknesses: Self-evaluation can share the original model's blind spots
references: Madaan et al., Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

patterns.name: Planner-Executor
patterns.description: A planning component creates an ordered plan and an executor carries out the individual steps.
patterns.intent: Separate high-level planning from detailed execution for complex multi-step tasks.
when_to_use: The task contains multiple dependent steps.
The execution order matters.
The plan can be evaluated before expensive execution begins.
when_not_to_use: The task is a single-step operation.
The plan changes so frequently that planning provides little value.
weaknesses: Planning adds an extra model step

patterns.name: Multi-Agent Debate
patterns.description: Multiple agents independently analyze a problem and then compare or debate their conclusions.
patterns.intent: Improve reasoning robustness by exposing a decision to independent perspectives and disagreement.
when_to_use: There are multiple plausible hypotheses.
Independent perspectives can reveal blind spots.
Conflicting evidence needs explicit comparison.
when_not_to_use: The task is simple and deterministic.
The additional model calls are not justified.
Agents would all have identical information and reasoning.
weaknesses: Requires careful role and evidence design

patterns.name: Router
patterns.description: A routing component classifies an incoming request and directs it to the most appropriate specialized workflow or agent.
patterns.intent: Select the appropriate capability based on the type or characteristics of the request.
when_to_use: Requests fall into distinct categories.
Different categories need different tools or prompts.
Specialized workflows outperform a single general workflow.
when_not_to_use: All requests require the same workflow.
The categories are poorly defined or overlap heavily.
strengths: Easy to extend with new routes
references: General routing architecture for agentic systems

patterns.name: RAG
patterns.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves relevant external knowledge and supplies it to an LLM before generation.
patterns.intent: Ground model outputs in project-specific or external information that is not reliably contained in model parameters.
when_to_use: The task depends on private or changing knowledge.
Answers need evidence from documents or a knowledge base.
The relevant information is too large to place entirely in the prompt.
when_not_to_use: The task requires no external knowledge.
The required information is already small and fully available in the request.
references: Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

patterns.name: Tool-Use
patterns.description: An LLM invokes structured external tools to perform actions or retrieve information that the model cannot reliably perform internally.
patterns.intent: Extend agent capabilities with deterministic functions, APIs, databases, search, or other external systems.
when_to_use: External information or actions are required.
A deterministic API or function can perform the task more reliably.
The model needs capabilities outside text generation.
when_not_to_use: The task can be completed accurately without tools.
A tool would introduce unnecessary risk or complexity.

patterns.name: Hierarchical Agents
patterns.description: A higher-level agent coordinates specialized lower-level agents or sub-workflows.
patterns.intent: Manage complex work by delegating subtasks to specialized agents under a coordinating agent.
when_to_use: The problem naturally decomposes into specialized domains.
Different subtasks require different capabilities.
A coordinator is needed to combine specialist outputs.
when_not_to_use: The problem is small enough for one agent.
Delegation overhead outweighs specialization benefits.

patterns.name: Critic-Refine
patterns.description: A separate critic evaluates an artifact against an explicit rubric and sends structured feedback to a generator for revision.
patterns.intent: Improve generated artifacts using an independent evaluation stage.
when_to_use: There is a clear quality rubric.
Generated artifacts such as code, plans, or documents can be reviewed.
Independent evaluation is useful.
when_not_to_use: No meaningful evaluation criteria exist.
The artifact is trivial or deterministic.
strengths: Works well for code and plans

patterns.name: Map-Reduce / Parallel Workers
patterns.description: A task is split into independent subtasks that can be processed in parallel and then combined into a final result.
patterns.intent: Increase throughput and reduce elapsed time for independent units of work.
when_to_use: Subtasks are sufficiently independent.
Results can be combined after parallel processing.
Latency benefits from concurrency.
when_not_to_use: Subtasks have strong sequential dependencies.
The aggregation step is as expensive as sequential execution.
references: MapReduce programming model and parallel agent architectures

patterns.name: Human-in-the-Loop
patterns.description: The workflow pauses at a defined decision point and requests human input, approval, clarification, or correction before continuing.
patterns.intent: Keep humans responsible for ambiguous, high-impact, or approval-sensitive decisions.
when_to_use: The system needs clarification.
A decision has significant business or operational impact.
Human approval is explicitly required.
when_not_to_use: The workflow is fully deterministic and low risk.
Human intervention would create unnecessary bottlenecks.
weaknesses: Requires durable state and UI/API integration

patterns.name: Evaluator-Optimizer
patterns.description: An evaluator measures an output against defined criteria and an optimizer repeatedly improves it until it meets a bounded quality threshold.
patterns.intent: Systematically optimize an artifact using measurable evaluation feedback.
when_to_use: Quality can be measured against explicit criteria.
Iterative improvement provides meaningful gains.
A stopping threshold or retry limit can be defined.
when_not_to_use: There is no reliable evaluation signal.
Iteration would not materially improve the output.
strengths: Useful for plans and generated artifacts
